To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) esophageal variceal bleeding (EVB) occurs in 8% of sorafenib-treated hepatocellular carcinoma patients with advanced or intermmediate disease, (2) EVB is predicted by the presence of neoplastic portal thrombosis (PVT), and (3) EVB can be prevented in sorafenib patients with PVT by propranolol.

(1) UGE screening is warranted before starting sorafenib in patients with advanced HCC, as it identifies patients at high risk of bleeding during sorafenib therapy; (2) the presence of nPVT is the strongest risk factor for bleeding from EVs during sorafenib; and (3) bleeding from EVs occurs in a significant proportion of patients treated with sorafenb, and is associated with poor prognosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of neoplastic portal venous thrombosis is the most important predictor of bleeding in patients with HCC receiving sorafenib.
sorafenib treatment is safe in HCC patients without EVs and in those with small EVs.
the prevalence of esophageal variaces in sorafenib treated patients is higher than in the general population and is related to the presence of nPVT.
